points.description: States that an ESN is a type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) that has at least one cyclic/feedback connection (both the RNN classification and the cyclic/feedback connection must be stated).
points.partial_credit: Only one of the two (RNN, or cyclic/feedback connection) stated precisely earns no marks; both are required.

points.description: States that only the weights of the output layer are updated/trained during learning (other weights are not trained).
Difference 1: ESN has feedback (recurrent) connections whereas a FF NN does not (signals flow only forward).
Difference 2: ESN can approximate dynamic systems whereas a FF NN cannot.

rubric.notes: Each point needs an explicit, correct statement using the terms recurrent/feedback (cyclic) connection, output layer weights, and dynamic systems. Vague wording (e.g. "ESN has memory", "ESN is more complex") earns nothing, and a wrong statement inside a point (e.g. saying all weights are trained, or that ESN is feed-forward) cancels that point. Total is the sum of points earned, out of 2.
